newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans no domestic borrowing in April.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans no domestic borrowing in April.

text.p: Turkey's treasury will not borrow from domestic markets in April because of its favourable cash flow table, State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Tuesday.

"The treasury has successfully raised 133 trillion in its two-year inflation indexed bond auction at a lower cost. It will not borrow in the rest of this month," Soylemez, responsible for the treasury and privatisation, told Reuters.

The treasury auctioned 133 trillion lira of inflation-indexed, two-year bonds at 22 percent risk premium on Tuesday, compared to 109.8 trillion lira sale and 24 percent risk premium in the previous auction, held on April 1.
Tuesday's auction with Wednesday's value date helps the treasury meet its domestic debt repayment of about 200 trillion lira on Wednesday.
Soylemez said the treasury would borrow at better terms in coming months beacuse of its tax income and lessened domestic debt repayments.
"The treasury will continue inflation-indexed auctions in the summer months. Our target is to extend the maturity," he added.
